feedback_request.integration_feedback: Report max_error on oval, s-bend and slalom against iteration 5 (0.0612, 0.0628, 0.0613). Say whether line_loss_events stayed at 0. Say whether the forward row produced earlier or more aggressive steering, and whether steering_oscillation rose above about 0.15 on slalom. Say whether the controller needed kp or kd retuning for the longer lookahead. If the floor is unchanged, say so explicitly, because that rules out lookahead.

intent: Single-lever test of sensor lookahead against the iteration 5 baseline. The sensor row moves from y=0.03 to y=0.06 m, ahead of the axle. Span ±0.05 m, 16 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.035 m, body and mass 0.6 kg are unchanged. This isolates whether earlier sensing lowers the max_error floor near 0.061 and recovers oval and s-bend progress.
learning: Pending race of iteration 6. If max_error falls below about 0.058 with 0 line losses, keep y=0.06 and tune span toward ±0.055. If the floor is unchanged, lookahead is ruled out and the next geometry test is a wider track (0.16 m) or a 0.008 m footprint, since those are the remaining untested geometry levers.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 5 show a stable pattern. Line losses are removed by a sensor span of ±0.05 m or wider, but max_error stays pinned at 0.0601 to 0.0628 on every track. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), so body width cannot raise it within range. Oval progress is 0.115 in every design, so the failure point is almost fixed regardless of geometry. Four geometry levers have now failed to move the floor: span (±0.04 to ±0.06), wheel_track (0.10 to 0.12), wheel_radius (0.03 to 0.035) and mass (0.8 to 0.6). Mass 0.6 gave a small gain on slalom max_error and a small loss on s-bend, with no net change, so it is not the lever. Iteration 5 (±0.05, 16 mm, y=0.03, 0.12 m track, 0.035 radius, 0.6 kg) is the current best-controlled baseline, with score 26.99. The only geometry lever not yet isolated against this baseline is the sensor row's forward position. Iteration 0 used y=0.05 but with a different span and footprint, so its result was confounded. I therefore move the row forward from y=0.03 to y=0.06 and change nothing else. The hypothesis is that more lookahead gives the controller earlier warning of the bend, so the robot starts correcting before reaching the 0.06 m edge. Expected result: max_error on oval and s-bend falls below about 0.058 with line_loss_events at 0. If the floor stays at 0.060 to 0.062, sensor lookahead is also ruled out, and the next geometry test should be a much wider track (0.16 m) or a smaller footprint (0.008 m) to sharpen the edge signal.
